key_insight: MOTIF improves out-of-distribution materials property prediction by using LLMs to propose chemical taxonomies rather than predict numerical properties directly.
engineering_relevance: The framework could improve screening of unfamiliar perovskite chemistries by making property models more robust to shifts in material families.
method: Generate candidate material taxonomies with LLMs.
Retain taxonomies that improve training-only pseudo-OOD validation.
Apply invariant feature selection within accepted taxonomies and combine predictions through gated aggregation.
evidence_signal: On 2D halide perovskites, mean OOD bandgap MAE fell from 0.122 to 0.111 eV; frozen dev/test evaluation also showed smaller gains, with transfer evaluated on 3D perovskite solar cell efficiencies and Matbench datasets.
watch_item: Taxonomy selection must remain training-only, and gains on unseen chemistries depend on how well pseudo-OOD validation represents deployment shifts.
paper_title: MOTIF: LLM-Defined Material Taxonomies for OOD Property Prediction via Invariant Feature Selection
